Here's why: --- # 1️⃣ Rust is memory safe 🛡️ One of the advantages of Rust is its **memory safety without garbage collection**. This **reduces overhead** and ensures a *fast, smooth experience*—exactly what you need for a kernel like Linux. # 2️⃣ Developers love Rust 🧑‍💻 According to [this article](https://travis.media/blog/why-rust/), Rust is **a favorite among programmers for its unique combination of performance, safety, and concurrency, ranking as the top most desired language for subsequent years now in Stack Overflow surveys.** # 3️⃣ Rust is simply faster 🚀 If you've ever used Rust yourself, you probably noticed a *significant* boost in performance. This is because Rust is a newer language compared to C and C++.
